questions.question: Explain the difference between a business aim and a business objective, giving an example of each.

points.text: An aim is a general, long-term goal - e.g. 'to become the most popular cafe in the city'. An objective is a specific, measurable target that supports the aim - e.g. 'to achieve a 20% market share of city centre coffee sales within 12 months'. Aims give direction; objectives provide measurable milestones.

questions.question: Write a SMART objective for a new coffee shop that has been trading for 6 months.

points.text: 'Increase monthly revenue from 8,000 GBP to 12,000 GBP within 6 months by introducing a loyalty scheme and extending opening hours to 7pm.' This is Specific (increase revenue), Measurable (from 8k to 12k), Achievable (through specific actions), Relevant (supports growth), Time-bound (within 6 months).

questions.question: Explain why a business's objectives might change as it moves from start-up to an established company.

points.text: Start-up: survival is the priority - covering costs, building a customer base, establishing the brand. Established: survival is assured, so objectives shift to profit maximisation, growth, increasing market share. Mature: may focus on ethical objectives or diversification as competition increases. Objectives evolve as circumstances change.
